title: Slope and Rate of Change
seo_title: Algebra I Slope and Rate of Change Worksheets (TEKS A.3A, A.3B)
standard_text: A.3A determine the slope of a line given a table of values, a graph, two points on the line, and an equation written in various forms, including y = mx + b, Ax + By = C, and y − y1 = m(x − x1); A.3B calculate the rate of change of a linear function represented tabularly, graphically, or algebraically in context of mathematical and real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Algebra I slope worksheets for Texas TEKS A.3A and A.3B: slope from graphs, two points, tables and equations, zero and undefined slope, and rate of change in context. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Slope = change in y ÷ change in x = (y2 − y1) ÷ (x2 − x1).
  • Up to the right: positive slope. Down to the right: negative. Horizontal: 0. Vertical: undefined.
  • In y = mx + b the slope is m. In Ax + By = C the slope is −A ÷ B.
  • The rate of change gives the units: dollars per week, feet per hour.

Examples

Example

(2, 5) and (6, 17)

(17 − 5) ÷ (6 − 2) = 12 ÷ 4

Answer: slope 3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Flipping rise and runChange in y goes on top.
Subtracting in different ordersUse the same point first in both.
Dividing the values instead of the changesUse differences, not the numbers themselves.

items.q: A line goes up from left to right. What sign is its slope?
items.e: Going up from left to right means a positive slope.

items.q: A line goes down from left to right. What sign is its slope?
items.e: Going down from left to right means a negative slope.

items.q: What is the slope of a horizontal line?
items.e: A horizontal line has no rise: slope 0.

items.q: What is the slope of a vertical line?
items.e: A vertical line has no run, and you cannot divide by 0: the slope is undefined.

items.q: Which line is steeper: slope 3 or slope 1/2?
items.e: A bigger slope (ignoring the sign) is steeper. Slope 3 is steeper.

items.q: Which line is steeper: slope −4 or slope 2?
items.e: Compare the sizes: 4 is bigger than 2, so slope −4 is steeper (it goes down).

items.q: Two right triangles are drawn under the same line. One has rise 2 and run 3. The other has run 9. What is its rise?
items.e: The triangles are similar, so rise ÷ run is the same: 2/3 = 6/9. The rise is 6.

items.q: Why is the slope the same between any two points on a line?
items.e: Any two slope triangles on the same line have the same angles. The slope triangles are similar, so rise ÷ run is equal.

items.q: A line has slope 2/5. If you go right 10, how far up do you go?
items.e: Rise = slope × run = 2/5 × 10 = 4.

items.q: A line has slope −3. If you go right 2, what happens to y?
items.e: Change in y = −3 × 2 = −6. It goes down 6.

items.q: A hill rises 30 feet over a run of 150 feet. What is its slope?
A ramp rises 2 feet over 24 feet. What is its slope?
A plane goes down 3,000 feet over 15 miles of distance. What is the rate of change?
items.e: Change ÷ distance = −3,000 ÷ 15 = −200 feet per mile.

items.q: The temperature goes from 50°F at 1 p.m. to 62°F at 4 p.m. What is the rate of change?
A line goes through (2, 5) with slope 3. Which point is also on the line?
A line goes through (0, 4) with slope −1/2. Which point is also on the line?
items.e: Go right 2 and down 1: (0 + 2, 4 − 1) = (2, 3).

items.q: Two lines are parallel. One has slope 5/3. What is the slope of the other?
items.e: Parallel lines have the same slope: 5/3.

items.q: Which pair of points gives a slope of 1?
Ana says the slope through (1, 2) and (4, 8) is 3/6. What did she do wrong?
items.e: Rise = 6 and run = 3, so the slope is 6/3 = 2. She divided run by rise.

items.q: Ben finds the slope through (1, 7) and (3, 3) as (3 − 7) ÷ (1 − 3) = 2. What is the correct slope?
items.e: Subtract in the same order: (3 − 7) ÷ (3 − 1) = −4 ÷ 2 = −2.
